title: On the validity of retrospective predictive performance evaluation procedures in just-in-time software defect prediction
does: Empirically studies how the choice of waiting time (and the resulting one-sided label noise in clean labels) affects validity of retrospective JIT-SDP evaluation on 13 GitHub projects; finds waiting time has little impact on retrospective validity.
does_not: Proposes no learning method; does not model the probability that a provisionally-clean commit is defective as a function of age; no delay-distribution estimation (Springer PDF blocked by bot challenge, so only abstract read).

title: A Practical Human Labeling Method for Online Just-in-Time Software Defect Prediction (HumLa / ECo-HumLa)
does: Adds immediate human labeling of changes predicted defect-inducing on top of the waiting-time method; ECo-HumLa targets inspection at most confidently-predicted changes; 14 GitHub projects; shows waiting-time-only labeling underestimates performance.
does_not: Keeps the hard waiting-time rule for clean labels; no age-dependent soft relabelling or weighting of provisionally-clean commits; no discovery-delay distribution or truncation correction; relies on human effort rather than statistical correction.

title: Human-in-the-loop online just-in-time software defect prediction: What have we achieved and what do we still miss?
does: Identifies observed-label noise from waiting-time + BFC labelling and verification latency in O-JIT-SDP; proposes human-in-the-loop SQA feedback to improve label reliability and a k-fold distributed bootstrap evaluation framework.
does_not: No probabilistic model of residual defect probability vs commit age; no delay-distribution estimation; correction is via human feedback, not re-weighting.

title: Quantifying SZZ-induced evaluation bias in just-in-time defect prediction
does: Manually validated ground truth for 420 commits in 6 projects; PR-SZZ mislabels ~12% of commits (mostly false positives); recall drops 0.72->0.64 and precision 0.27->0.19 against manual truth; stratified weighted evaluation protocol.
does_not: Focuses on SZZ false positives, not time-dependent false negatives from undiscovered defects; offline, no online learning, no age-dependent weighting or delay distribution. (Read Research Square preprint version.)

does_not: Noise model is static (joint noisy/true label distribution), not a function of commit age or discovery delay; offline; removes rather than re-weights; no truncation-corrected estimate. (ACM PDF 403.)

title: Modeling delayed feedback in display advertising (DFM)
does: Joint model of conversion probability and (exponential) conversion delay fitted by EM; a not-yet-converted click is down-weighted according to elapsed time vs predicted delay, i.e. P(will convert | not converted by e) = p*S(e) / (1 - p + p*S(e)). (Model form confirmed via descriptions in FSIW/ES-DFM/Yasui-Kato full texts.)
does_not: Ad CVR, not JIT-SDP; delay distribution is parametric and estimated from right-CENSORED data where every click (the full at-risk cohort) is observed - not the right-TRUNCATED situation of JIT-SDP where defective commits are only known once discovered; no reverse-time product-limit estimator; no software prior.
queries_used: modeling delayed feedback in display advertising Chapelle

title: A Feedback Shift Correction in Predicting Conversion Rates under Delayed Feedback (FSIW)
does: Importance-weighting for feedback shift; estimates P(S=1|C=1,x,elapsed) and true-negative probabilities with auxiliary classifiers using elapsed time as feature; proves consistency.
does_not: Requires a labelled reference window and auxiliary classifiers; CVR domain; no right-truncation estimator; no JIT-SDP.
queries_used: ti:"delayed feedback" AND ti:conversion

title: Capturing Delayed Feedback in Conversion Rate Prediction via Elapsed-Time Sampling (ES-DFM)
does: Models elapsed time as a distribution; importance weights per instance with fake-negative probability conditioned on elapsed time; streaming CVR.
does_not: CVR; fake-negative probability learned by a neural classifier rather than from a truncation-corrected nonparametric delay estimate; no SE application.

title: Asymptotically Unbiased Estimation for Delayed Feedback Modeling via Label Correction (DEFUSE) - full text
does: Two-step: infers probability that an observed negative is a fake negative, then corrects importance weights for four sample types; bi-distribution modelling of immediate vs delayed positives.
does_not: CVR; fake-negative probability learned by a model; no reverse-time/right-truncation estimator; no JIT-SDP. (Upgrade of ledger entry from abstract to full text.)

title: Real Negatives Matter: Continuous Training with Real Negatives for Delayed Feedback Modeling (DEFER)
does: Ingests duplicated real negatives after the attribution window plus importance sampling to keep observed distribution equal to true distribution.
does_not: CVR; relies on eventually-certain negatives after a fixed window (like a waiting time) rather than an age-dependent probability from an estimated delay law.

title: Unbiased Delayed Feedback Label Correction for Conversion Rate Prediction (ULC)
